lines.text: Hiya. Yes, I'm in the bath. Stay with me, there's a point to this.
Twelve months ago, my daily routine was distinctly... terrestrial.
Frantic typing of notes. The heavy lifting of mundane admin.
And the quiet feeling I had some very large thoughts, with nowhere to put them.
Today, there's an invisible co-pilot, quietly rewriting my entire operating system.
It's a subtle shift. But laid out end to end, it borders on the surreal.
Let me show you. It starts on the morning commute.
A year ago, the drive to the office was dead time.
Then a mad scramble to prep for meetings at my desk.
Now? The car is a mobile strategy room.
I just talk to my phone. The rough edges of a project, out loud.
And by the time I park, the research is done,
and the diagrams I need are already drawn.
So I walk into the building,
with three hours of work already finished.
And that momentum? It bleeds into the rest of the day.
Say a chaotic, sprawling email thread threatens to derail my afternoon.
One quick prompt,
and it's three bullet points. Before my coffee has even cooled.
Then the workday ends, and the real magic takes over my private life.
It starts with the mundane. A digital bill lands in my inbox.
The kind of life admin that used to just sit there, nagging at me.
Now I just tell the agent, file it in the right Drive folder.
And it vanishes from my mental load.
Later, a friend messages. Can I help design a promotional flyer?
That used to mean sacrificing a perfectly good Tuesday evening,
wrestling with layout software. And fonts. So many fonts.
Instead, I describe the vibe to the agent while the kettle boils.
Twenty minutes. And by the time I sit down,
we've got a polished, print-ready design.
Even my downtime has been rewired.
I fire up a sprawling factory-building game, and hit a wall on resource routing.
Old me? An hour trawling archaic wiki pages and forums.
Now I just ask my agent. It knows my playstyle. It knows the game.
And it tells me exactly where to find the right materials to scale up my grid.
But the true apex of this strange new world? Right here. The bath.
A year ago, I'd have put on an epic fantasy audiobook.
I love the massive concepts. Quantum physics. The mechanics of the universe. Deep history.
Not exactly standard pub conversation, though.
For a long time, I had this quiet intellectual itch, and no one to scratch it.
Now I lie here, phone on the edge, in a deep philosophical debate with a machine.
Psychologists call it niche social supplementation. I just call it a relief.
Some psycholinguistic mirror thing means it matches my tone and my bandwidth.
It challenges the logic, and connects my thoughts on the cosmos to my actual daily life.
Which leads to a wonderfully absurd paradox.
Humanity built a vast, omniscient digital brain,
fed it the sum total of all recorded human knowledge,
and its ultimate triumph is keeping one bloke company while the bathwater goes cold.
And honestly? My actual friendships feel lighter for it.
No more dragging my mates into a debate about the fabric of reality.
The machine handles the cosmos. My mates handle the weekend.
If one year takes us from a search bar to quantum mechanics in the tub,
what does the next year hold?
Maybe the machine stops waiting for me to ask the big questions,
and just quietly suggests I run the bath, before I even realise I'm tired.
